column1: # The behaviour baseline: every CLI verb the command enum knows, in every
# output mode it supports, every --help, the generated references, the MCP
# tool specs and the config/filter surface — captured against the SAME pinned
# demo store as ../manifest.tsv, by the SAME script
# Why a second directory rather than more rows in ../manifest.tsv: that file's
# rows are embedded into the docs site verbatim
# (crates/tasqx-cli/src/fixtures.rs's `screens!` macro), held equal to it in
# A row added there ships in the guide whether or not it belongs there; a row
# added HERE captures the same way without ever reaching `tasqx docs`. See
# docs/maintainers/behaviour-baseline.md for what this corpus proves and does
# Rows here do not repeat what ../manifest.tsv already captures for a verb —
# this file only ADDS coverage: the modes and verbs that manifest never
# exercises. The baseline for a verb already in the site's default-mode
# capture is that fixture plus whatever rows below add for it.
# Columns are identical to ../manifest.tsv (name, kind, cols, rows, args,
# keys, stdin), with two more `kind`s docs-capture.sh understands:
#   pipe-plain      like `pipe`, but TASQX_FORCE_COLOR/TERM are left unset —
#                   the render path a script or agent actually gets piping
#                   tasqx with no terminal behind it, which every `pipe`/
#                   `pipe-mut` row in EITHER manifest forces to the coloured
#                   terminal layout instead (docs-capture.sh's own comment on
#                   `capture_pipe`). Untested before this file: a change that
#                   only shows up off the colour path had no fixture watching
#   pipe-plain-mut  `pipe-plain` against a copy of the store, for the same
# `<verb>-json` / `<verb>-card` / `<verb>-plain` name the output mode; a bare
# verb name is its default-mode capture where ../manifest.tsv has none.
# Ids reused below (51, 49, the check/annotation/memory-doc uuids) are the
# same ones ../manifest.tsv's rows already use, so a fresh reader who has read
# that file recognises them; every mutating row still runs against its own
# copy of the store, so the reuse is only for the reader.
# --- --json, for read verbs ../manifest.tsv only shows in the human table
# (task.brief and memory.search stay out: their JSON carries an FTS `rank`,
# platform-dependent bm25 digits per ../manifest.tsv's own header) ---
# --- --card / --card --ascii, the four verbs that take it ---
# --- pipe-plain: the render path with no terminal behind it (see the `kind`
# --- default-mode captures for verbs ../manifest.tsv does not show at all.
# `config set`/`config unset`/`theme set` and `config path`/`config store` are
# deliberately absent: the first three write config.toml, which (unlike
# tasks.db) this harness does not copy per row, so a mutating config row would
# make every row after it depend on manifest order; the last two print an
# absolute path (TASQX_CONFIG_DIR / TASQX_DB), which is this machine's, the
# same reason ../manifest.tsv drops `about`. `setup --list` uses a fixed,
# nonexistent --home so its ITEM/STATUS table never reads a real machine's
# ~/.claude. `memory import` names a real path in this repo
# (docs/maintainers/dependency-policy.md) rather than a scratch file: the
# command run from the repo root does not echo it back (checked), and the
# imported prose is real content worth a fixture over a throwaway string.
# `completions bash`/`completions powershell` stand in for the other three
# shells clap_complete emits (elvish, fish, zsh): same code path, different
# grammar, not worth five near-identical fixtures.
# `export` and `memory add` are absent too, found by this file's own
# determinism proof (two captures, diffed): the demo store's one RUNNING task
# is left running by a live `tasqx start` inside demo-store.py, which mints a
# real event id at the pin instant, and `export`'s full-store dump prints that
# id's random tail; `memory add`'s echo prints the fresh doc UUID it just
# minted, with no short-id form the way `add-echo`'s task id has. Same class
# as `api task.add`'s exclusion in ../manifest.tsv, one layer further in. ---
